subject: HIN
label: Grade 09
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 09 Hindi, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Prose and travel writing
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Prose and travel writing', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: read and summarise. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Prose and travel writing' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and summarise, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: गद्यांश पढ़ें; मुख्य भाव एक वाक्य में लिखें; प्रश्नों के उत्तर गद्यांश के शब्दों में दें; एक उचित शीर्षक सुझाएँ। Method: Model run for 'Prose and travel writing'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Read and summarise: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, warm up: say or read the example aloud twice, slowly. Cover it and say it again from memory.
Step 2, find the pattern: underline the word, ending or sentence part that 'Prose and travel writing' is about. Say in your own words why it is there.
Step 3, change one thing: swap one word, name or number in the example and say the new version aloud.
Step 4, write two new lines of your own that do the same job. Keep them short and true to your life.
Step 5, swap with a partner: read each other's lines, circle one thing to fix, and fix it.
Step 6, own it: read your final lines to the class or teacher. Standard: read and summarise.

When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Unseen passage and comprehension) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
